thesis_statement: NVIDIA supplies the dominant accelerated-computing platform (GPUs, networking and CUDA software) for AI training and inference; revenue doubled year over year to $96.2B in Q2 FY27 with 75% gross margins, and guidance points to further growth as the Vera Rubin generation ramps.

base.summary: Data-center revenue keeps growing sequentially through the Vera Rubin ramp with gross margins in the mid-70s.

bull.summary: More frontier labs, sovereign AI and physical-AI demand extend the build-out beyond current expectations.
drivers: multiple frontier labs scaling in parallel

bear.summary: Customers slow AI capex or shift to custom chips, and revenue growth turns negative from a very high base.

key_risks: Customer concentration: revenue depends on a small number of hyperscalers and AI labs whose capex can pause.
Competition from custom accelerators built by its largest customers.
Export-control and geopolitical risk on China and other markets.

fundamental: Revenue guidance for a quarter falls below the prior quarter's actual revenue.
Gross margin falls below 70% for two consecutive quarters.
